name: Three-tier web application
summary: A familiar web stack: browser, reverse proxy, application, relational data, cache, and background e-mail. An editable reference pattern.

name: Multi-tenant SaaS
summary: A shared application with explicit tenant context, identity, subscription billing, and asynchronous notifications. Illustrates shared infrastructure, not a complete tenant-isolation design.

name: E-commerce platform
summary: A storefront with catalog, cart, checkout, external payment processing, and asynchronous fulfillment. Service boundaries are illustrative and can be consolidated.

name: Background job processing
summary: An API and scheduler feed workers through a queue, with retry and dead-letter paths. Useful for document conversion, reports, and long-running tasks.

name: Headless content publishing
summary: Editors publish through a CMS while an independent delivery frontend consumes a content API. Media uses object storage and a CDN; publishing jobs refresh delivery artifacts.

name: Real-time collaboration
summary: Two real-time servers share durable messages and fan-out work while clients keep WebSocket connections. Includes presence, attachments, and offline notifications.

name: Analytics data pipeline
summary: Operational events and batch extracts flow through ingestion, raw storage, transformation, and a warehouse to dashboards. A logical reference for analytical workloads.

name: Umbraco local Cluster
summary: The checked-in Umbraco demo: CM + two CDs, YARP, SQL-backed cache, shared filesystem media, and Aspire tools. Local development; the Astro frontend is independent of Umbraco.
